mappings.note: Two dice: even sum by parity pairing, and even product taken as 36 - 9 odd-odd pairs. Compound dice event plus a complement, both inside LO-4.

Eight named cards are removed, so the reduced n(S) = 44 and the revised suit counts are the work (C-8.1-LO-4); the four probabilities are simple events (LO-3); and part (i) comes out 0 because both black queens were removed, an impossible event (LO-2).
Part (i) is P(not red) = 1 - x/20, the complement rule with an unknown (LO-4); part (ii) solves the ratio condition for the favourable red count (C-8.1-LO-4).

Two spins give an ordered-pair space of 36 that must be organised by first coordinate before a/b > 1 can be counted, so C-8.1-LO-4 leads; LO-4 carries the two-stage structure. The spinner is neither card, die nor coin, which LO-4's wording does not anticipate.

Single draw from 25 cards. Part (i) needs 8 + 5 - 1 to avoid double-counting 15, i.e. the addition rule, for which the frame has no outcome; LO-3 is the honest home since the experiment is one equally likely draw.
A die rolled twice: no 5 either time (5 x 5 of 36) and exactly one 5. Compound dice events, LO-4.
One ball from 15: number 8, even, multiple of 3, solid-and-even. Four simple events on an unchanged sample space, LO-3; no complement or multi-stage structure.

Single draw from 100 voters read off a two-way table (LO-3), but parts (i) and (v) need a union with the overlap removed and a double negation counted as 100 - (8 + 20), which is complement/compound work (LO-4).

Full production is the complement of 'both generators fail', so P = 1 - 0.007. A pure complement-rule item working from given probabilities rather than counts, LO-4; the two single-failure figures are deliberate distractors.
Trip completed is the complement of 'both engines fail', P = 1 - 0.013. Complement rule on given probabilities, LO-4.
Unimpeded response is the complement of 'both routes clogged', P = 1 - 0.03. Complement rule, LO-4; the individual route probabilities are not needed.
Mostly simple events over 15 balls (LO-3), but part (ii) 'a number greater than fifteen' has no favourable outcome and yields 0, which is the impossible-event end of the probability range (LO-2).

Three of the four parts are explicit complements - greater than three as 1 - P(three or less), no blank half, not a double (LO-4) - resting on the 28-tile double-six sample space that must be enumerated (C-8.1-LO-4).
Percentages treated as frequencies out of 100 and summed over the stated child-count bands; part (iv) simply compares the three results. Simple events, LO-3, with no complement taken.

Geometric probability: the dartboard answers are ratios of circular areas, not counts of equally likely outcomes, so LO-3 would misdescribe the method. Cited at competency level because the frame has no outcome for area-based probability.
Area ratios of triangles and a trapezoid against a rectangle. Same gap as the dartboard item: no outcome covers geometric probability, so the competency is the only honest code.
Blood-group frequencies give simple events for types O and A-or-B (LO-3); parts (iii) and (iv) are 'neither A nor O' and an explicit use of the complement (LO-4).
One school from 1000, with favourable counts pooled across grouped classes. Simple events on an unchanged sample space, LO-3.

The sample space is 210 lattice points defined by inequalities, and the favourable sets are points lying on given graphs, so identifying and counting the sample space is the work (C-8.1-LO-4); LO-3 gives the ratios.
Discrete frequency distribution of hospital stays; each part pools frequencies for exactly, less than, at most and at least. Simple events, LO-3, all counted directly rather than by complement.
Four parts are direct counts of odd numbers with extra conditions (LO-3); part (v) 'odd and not a multiple of 11' is taken as the complement within the odd numbers (LO-4).
One driver from 1000 read off an age-by-accidents two-way table; each part pools cells of that table. Simple events, LO-3.
Geometric probability by area on an archery target, which no outcome covers, hence the competency; part (iv) is additionally taken as the complement of part (ii), 1 - 11/18, hence LO-4.

Empirical probability from 2400 successes in 4000 trials. The whole frame - goal, competency and every outcome - speaks only of THEORETICAL probability, so no outcome fits an experimental relative frequency; cited at competency level rather than stretching LO-3's 'equally likely outcomes'.
Empirical probability 207/460 from past at-bats. Same gap as the Remdesivir item: experimental probability has no outcome anywhere in this frame.
